pride_data.title: Crosslinking Interaction Network of Human Mitochondria
pride_data.projectDescription: Isolated human mitochondria underwent DSSO crosslinking. Following treatment, the mitochondria were separated into soluble and insoluble fractions. Both fractions were then subjected to multidimensional fractionation, including SCX and hSAX. The fractionated peptides were subsequently analyzed using CL-MS. FDR-based error estimation facilitated the creation of a comprehensive mitochondrial interaction network, revealing novel protein-protein interactions.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Isolated mitochondria from K-562 cells were treated with the membrane-permeable crosslinker DSSO. The mitochondria were lysed, and the material was split into soluble and insoluble fractions. Both fractions were digested separately and subjected to multidimensional fractionation, including SCX and hSAX. The fractionated samples were then used for CL-MS acquisition. Comprehensive and stringent error control resulted in a confident interaction network of proteins across the human mitochondria.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The obtained raw files were mass-shift corrected, and the recalibrated files were used for XiSearch along with a FASTA file as the database. Utilizing robust XiFDR error control, a comprehensive crosslinking dataset was generated.
